item.title: No rest for Michigan basketball as Thanksgiving week brings busy schedule
item.description: The schedule is about to heat up for Michigan basketball. The Wolverines had few days off this week, with a six-day gap on the nonconference slate. But they'll make up for that in a hurry, with Michigan (3-) playing at least four – and potentially five – games in an eight-day stretch to close out November. That begins with a matchup against Villanova (3-2) on Saturday, Nov. 21 (7 p.m., Fox), at Xfinity Mobile Arena, home of the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers . It's a rematch of, among other games, last December's blowout by the Wolverines in Ann Arbor. Much as U-M has, Villanova has turned over its roster in its second season under coach Kevin Willard, with senior Tyler Perkins as the only returning player from last year's meeting. STEP IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION: Michigan basketball finding its identity, forged by foe's speed "It's becoming less and less where there's real continuity in programs year to year," said U-M coach Mike Boynton Jr. With the season still in its opening month, Boynton said he generally likes to focus practices in extended stretches like this past week on self-improvement − working on rotations, installing schemes and identifying solutions to early problems – rather than focusing on scouting reports on opponents. But this week, an illness went through the team in recent days, leaving a number of players were limited or held out as a result. "It's been more individual stuff as opposed to team, which I hate because I would love to have used the time more productively with our whole group," Boynton said. "Just wasn't really an option this time for us." Some of those individual focuses included more reps for Joseph Hartmann, a freshman wing, who returned to the court for the first time in a month Tuesday. Boynton said Thursday's practice would give the team "a little bit better indication" of where his conditioning is, but there's a chance he's available this weekend. U-M also continues to work on Jalen Reed's conditioning. The LSU transfer suffered season-ending leg injuries the past two years and was held out last week against Marquette after he felt a bit of soreness. He's expected to be available this weekend as well. As for the matchup, despite the roster shuffle, the Wildcats have at least one familiar face: Devin Royal – a three-year player at Ohio State and former teammate of Roddy Gayle Jr. – who leads 'Nova at 14.8 points per game and is second at 7.4 rebounds. item.title: ‘Can you blame him?’ – NFL fans defend Al Michaels after Texans vs. Colts snoozefest
item.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Al Michaels has come under a lot of scrutiny this season for his commentary on Amazon Prime’s broadcast of Thursday Night Football. At 82 years old, Michaels is working into the very back end of his career in NFL broadcasting, which has clearly led to some underwhelming performances up in the booth. Fans have expressed their disappointment with some of his play-calling on a number of occasions. Thursday night’s game between the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts once again saw a mellow Michaels in the booth. However, on this occasion, NFL fans jumped to his defense following what was one of the most boring games of the season. NFL fans defend Al Michaels after boring Thursday Night Football game The Colts are now seeing out their season after trading away most of their star players. That was on full display on Thursday evening as the Texans only gave up three points in what was never a real contest in Texas. Despite Michaels’ commentary lacking any enthusiasm, NFL fans were largely accepting, given the lack of spark on the field. ‘If you watched the game, this is the interest level he should have had. It was abysmal !! Horrible game to watch,’ responded one fan on X. ‘Do you blame him?? I lost interest in the game as soon as it started,’ added another. The game ended 26-3 to the Texans, with Amazon’s crew taking aim at Michaels during the game with a dig at the amount of vegetables he consumes. The level of interest surrounding the game on Thursday was clearly at an all-time low. ‘The game deserved that level of emotion…’ another NFL fan replied. ‘Just stop. You want him to get excited over that? Are you insane?’ said another. There have been a number of exciting Thursday Night Football games this season, but this week’s was not one of those. ‘In his defense, he was watching this abysmal game at the time,’ replied one NFL fan. item.title: Drake Allen went from high school manager to Motor City Cruise standout
item.description: For most people, getting cut by your junior varsity basketball team represents the end of their hoops dreams. But for Drake Allen, it was the beginning. The Motor City Cruise guard couldn't imagine life without basketball, so he became the team manager during his sophomore year at Westlake High School in Eagle Mountain, Utah. That meant picking up towels, running the scoreboard, keeping stats, rebounding basketballs during warmups and practice and, if he was lucky, stepping in and playing if they needed an extra guy. "I had a moment that sophomore year where I decided, how much do I love the game? " Allen said. "Am I going to be a manager? And if I was a manager the rest of my life and eventually a coach, that’s what I was gonna be. Just decided to stick around the game as long as I could and it ended up working out." BEST IN THE WEST? How a battered Pistons team solved Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs Thankfully for Allen, he underwent a growth spurt and the rest of his path began to click into place, going from around 5 feet 10 when he was initially cut to 6-4 en route to the Detroit Pistons ' G League affiliate. He played two years at the junior college level before transferring to mid-majors Southern Utah, Utah Valley and then finally two years at Utah State, before joining the Pistons' summer league team this past offseason. Now, he's off to a strong start with the Cruise and proving that there's still more ahead for his basketball journey, which once looked destined for the sideline. "Being able to be a little bit bigger, a little bit more athletic, that all came with time," He said. "But that first year, being able to grow my mind and my love for basketball, it grew even more. When someone takes something away from you, you realize how much it means to you. That’s what happened. Allowed me to become an even better player, I guess." Through five games with the Cruise during the G LEague's Tip-Off Tournament, Allen is averaging a team-high nine assists, along with 16.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals. His 45 assists are the most in franchise history through the first five games of the season, and also leads all G League rookies. Beyond passing the ball, Allen plays both end of the floor. During Las Vegas Summer League, his defensive effort and physicality shined. Allen comes from a sports family – his dad, Roque, played soccer in college, while his mom, Tamra, played volleyball. Allen recalls obsessively watching basketball as a young child, and every day after school. His love for the game only deepened as he grew older. "There’s something you can get better at better every day, and there’s not many things that you can continue to get better at over and over and add new things," he said. "You become obsessed with it, and I think that’s where the love comes from." He wasn't recruited in high school, so he began at Snow College in Ephraim, Utah. item.title: How can Ohio State football beat Nebraska in final regular-season road game?
item.description: Here are three keys for No. 14 Ohio State at Nebraska on Nov. 21: Play clean Penalties have plagued Ohio State throughout the season, especially away from Columbus. The Buckeyes have committed multiple false starts in each of their past three road games, including as many as five at Iowa last month. The trend continued at USC , where OSU mixed up cadences, leading to pre-snap issues during freshman quarterback Luke Fahey ’s first start. If they are going to finish above .500 on the road, the Buckeyes must avoid the self-inflicted mistakes that have put them behind the chains. Fahey’s added experience should help reduce communication breakdowns, but the Buckeyes need to be more disciplined across the board in a tough environment. Contain Anthony Colandrea The Buckeyes caught a break last week as Northwestern ’s Aidan Chiles remained sidelined with an injury, sparing them from facing one of the Big Ten’s best dual-threat quarterbacks. They won’t be as fortunate this week with Colandrea behind center for Nebraska. Colandrea leads the conference’s quarterbacks with 447 rushing yards. His legs pose a threat on scrambles as well as designed runs, making it paramount that the Buckeyes contain him in the pocket when plays break down. Colandrea has 22 runs of at least 10 yards, the second-most in the Big Ten behind Indiana running back Turbo Richard. Get off the field on third down Ohio State's struggles getting stops on third down have persisted for weeks, allowing teams to convert more than 40% of the time over the past four games. The defense has proven vulnerable even in third-and-long situations. The Buckeyes ranked 86 th in third-down defense through Week 11. They won’t find much reprieve at Nebraska, as the Cornhuskers can sustain drives. They rank 13 th in the Football Bowl Subdivision with a third-down conversion rate of 47.8%. The Buckeyes fared better against Northwestern, especially late in the game, with more traditional fronts with four down linemen and will look for the momentum to continue. Key matchup Ohio State offensive line vs. Nebraska defensive line It’s no coincidence Fahey put together arguably his best performance against Northwestern. After he was under duress on 32.3% of his dropbacks against Oregon and USC, he faced pressure on just 14.7% of his dropbacks against the Wildcats, according to Pro Football Focus. The protection allowed him to be more efficient and deliver at key junctures of the game. The Cornhuskers present a challenge up front as their 27 sacks are the fourth-most in the Big Ten, and they have posted multiple sacks in all but two games this year, though sack leader Jahsear Whittington will be unavailable. The pass rush puts the spotlight on the Buckeyes’ offensive line and whether they can continue to keep the pocket clean for Fahey after appearing more stable a week earlier. item.description: Declan Rice Roy Keane - Getty/GOAL Declan Rice has become Roy Keane and Bryan Robson-esque, former England star Paul Ince has told GOAL, with Arsenal’s Premier League title winner considered to be one of the top three midfielders in world football. Ex-Manchester City ace Rodri sits at the top of that talent tree, but an all-action Three Lions talisman has taken up a standing among the global elite. Record-breaking transfer to Arsenal Few could have predicted that would be the case when seeing Rice - who was released by Chelsea as a youngster - step out of the academy ranks at West Ham. No definitive role had been nailed down at that point, with regular game time being seen at centre-half . He eventually settled on a holding role in the middle of the park, with full potential being unlocked in the engine room. Rice captained the Hammers to Conference League glory in 2023. A matter of weeks later, with his stock having been on the rise for some time, a record-breaking £105 million ($138m) transfer to Arsenal was completed - as he became the most expensive British player in history . Game has changed with Gunners Further progression and development has been enjoyed in north London, with the affable 27-year-old now more of a buccaneering No.8 - for club and country - than a water-carrying six that is happy to win the ball and move it quickly on to others. There has been talk of Rice becoming a Ballon d’Or contender , having seen international colleague Harry Kane claim that prize in 2026 , with his value to any given cause clear to see - with a top-flight crown being captured with the Gunners last season. Widely considered to be one of the most complete midfielders in world football, Rice can claim to rub shoulders with the very best in the business - leading to comparisons being drawn with iconic box-to-box performers that once starred for Manchester United and England. item.title: UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma sounds off on NIL, recruiting
item.description: STORRS — For decades, UConn women’s basketball could walk into almost any gym in America and expect to be in the conversation for the nation’s best players. Now, as name, image and likeness (NIL) reshapes the sport’s power structure, coach Geno Auriemma says the Huskies are navigating a recruiting landscape where their prestige, winning and player development no longer carry the same weight. “We don't have cachet with guys that are getting a million dollars to go play someplace. They're getting the cachet,” Auriemma said after Thursday’s practice. “I just don't see the value of paying a high school kid a million dollars that hasn't dribbled the ball one time in college.” UConn falls in polls: UConn women’s basketball drops four spots in latest USA Today poll UConn by the numbers: Why UConn women's basketball needs more offense behind Sarah Strong Auriemma’s comments came as UConn’s 2027 recruiting class has taken shape in a way that would have been almost unthinkable for much of his tenure. The Huskies landed five-star guard Sydney Savoury, ESPN’s No. 9-ranked prospect, but missed on several of the nation’s top targets. No. 1 recruit Kaleena Smith narrowed her choices to USC, UCLA and Arizona State after UConn was widely viewed as a contender. No. 2 prospect Ivanna Wilson Manyacka committed to UCLA after the Huskies made her Top 5. No. 8 recruit Haylen Ayers chose Vanderbilt, while Hungarian standout Kinga Josepovits picked Duke. UConn was among the finalists for both prospects. UConn’s success has been built on being the destination for the top players in their respective recruiting classes. Whether that be Maya Moore, Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd or Tina Charles, the Huskies usually have no problem finding the best players in the nation to commit to playing in Storrs. But lately, the effects of NIL have been shown. According to 247Sports, UConn hasn’t reeled in a Top 10 recruiting class in the last two seasons. In 2026, the Huskies ranked 27th, and the year before, they were 17th. Auriemma and his staff have still gotten high-end talent, just not at the same volume. Last cycle, UConn signed five-star center Olivia Vukosa — the No. 2 ranked player in the country. But that was the only domestic recruit Auriemma brought into the program as he filled the rest of his roster with international players such as Jovana Popovic and Marine Dursus. As more schools pour resources into women’s basketball, Auriemma believes the shifting landscape is less an indictment of UConn and more of a reflection of the sport’s growth. “There's more schools that are investing more resources and the players are attracted to places that maybe in the past they weren't,” Auriemma said. “I think the growth of the game reflects that.” As the game changes, Auriemma has not altered his recruiting philosophy. item.description: Barcelona monitoring 17-year-old Girona defensive talent amid Premier League interest According to ESPN (h/t SPORT ), Barcelona have added Girona youngster Holmes Junior to their list of potential defensive targets as the club continue to assess their options at centre-back. The Catalans are closely following the 17-year-old’s progress, although they face competition from several Premier League clubs who are also monitoring his development. Strengthening the centre of defence has become a priority at Camp Nou, particularly after injuries have disrupted Hansi Flick’s options this season. While experienced options like Alessandro Bastoni are being considered , Barça continue to keep an eye on young talents with a long-term view, leading to their interest in the likes of Ruud Nijstad and now Holmes Junior. Already a first-team player at 17 Holmes Junior has enjoyed a steady rise to prominence since joining Girona’s academy in the summer of 2025. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Girona FC (@gironafc) The 17-year-old starlet spent time in Real Madrid’s youth system before making the move to Gimnastic in 2024 and subsequently signing for Girona, where he has continued to progress. In fact, such has been his development that Junior has already broken into the Girona first-team squad this season, making ten appearances – nine in La Liga 2 and one in Copa del Rey – with even a goal to his name. The youngster has also made four appearances for the Spain Under-18 national team. This potential and rapid ascent at Girona has put him on the radar of clubs looking to invest in promising young defenders, including Barcelona. item.title: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge
item.description: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge Despite racking up 43 shots and being denied by the woodwork on three separate occasions, Harry Kane still finds himself outside the top ten leading scorers in the Bundesliga. On the other hand, he leads the assists chart with seven from just nine outings. Quite impressively, this figure puts the Ballon d'Or winner two ahead of his total for the entirety of last season. Goals, however, usually flow from the very beginning. Last season, the net had bulged twelve times by this point – helped largely by a hat-trick that downed Leipzig on the opening day. By Kane’s own high standards and historical record in Germany, his return in the current campaign stands out as an anomaly. Underlying numbers, not least the absolutely relentless shot volume, do suggest that a change in fortune might just be around the corner. In part, you could explain this domestic dip by highlighting his tendency to occupy deeper positions and find the likes of Michael Olise and Luis Díaz on the charge. However, that is very much business as usual in Vincent Kompany’s enthralling system. Champions League statistics do tell a more familiar story, with four in as many matches reminding us of Kane’s potency at the highest level. One moment in particular sums up the England captain’s start: an inch-perfect pass that split Arsenal’s resolute defence in half and put the ball on a plate for Alphonso Davies to finish. As the Allianz Arena awaits the arrival of 1. FC Köln, it simply remains a case of when – not if – this unique goalscoring machine closes the gap to Patrik Schick and a revitalised Niclas Füllkrug.

item.title: Double injury blow for Arsenal! Mikel Arteta confirms setback as William Saliba & Bukayo Saka updates issued ahead of Newcastle trip
item.description: Arsenal FC v Hull City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal are bracing for a testing trip to St James' Park this weekend as Mikel Arteta manages a squad stretched by significant fitness issues. While one defensive pillar is finally closing in on a much-anticipated return to the fold, the Gunners have been rocked by fresh problems in midfield and attack. Midfield setback tempers Saliba fitness boost Arsenal head into Saturday night's domestic league clash against Newcastle with mixed injury news following the international break. Midfielder Martin Zubimendi has been ruled out for several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem while representing Spain against England last week, with a subsequent MRI scan confirming the damage. Meanwhile, talismanic forward Bukayo Saka remains unavailable as he continues his rehabilitation from a quad issue that has already sidelined him for five matches. Despite those absences, Arteta received a timely defensive boost on Friday as defender William Saliba is finally poised to join the matchday squad after recovering from a long-term back injury . Saliba has yet to make a competitive appearance this campaign, though he successfully stepped up his conditioning by featuring in two behind-closed-doors friendlies during the recent break. Arteta delivers mixed squad update before Newcastle Speaking to reporters during his pre-match briefing on Friday, Arteta confirmed that Saliba has done enough in training matches to earn a place in his plans for the trip north. "[Saliba] is ready, he’s in a good position. He played two games, he did really well," the Gunners boss said. However, Arteta struck a far more cautious tone when addressing Zubimendi's condition following his early exit on international duty. "[Zubimendi] is out," Arteta added. "Unfortunately he has a small issue in his hamstring. The MRI scan showed an issue there, he’s going to be out for a few weeks." Saka timeline stretches Gunners' attacking depth While Saliba's availability strengthens Arsenal's backline, coping without both Zubimendi and Saka simultaneously presents a stern test of the squad's resilience. Saka is not anticipated to return much before Christmas, leaving Arteta without a key attacking figure during a demanding period. Providing further clarity on the forward's recovery schedule, Arteta explained: "He had another scan. He’s evolving really well, but it looks like it’s going to be an eight-week injury. I think it’s four at the moment so still going to be a while until he’s back with the team." Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
